notes: A photograph of a printed keg collar lying on concrete, not flat artwork, so the small type is soft and the disc is slightly tilted.

The collar declares no single quantity. It preprints four sizes on four lines under the heading 'NET CONTENTS:', and the reading above joins those four lines in printed order with ' / '. Each of the four is transcribed as printed.

A hand-drawn stroke crosses the '7.7' of the third line, '7.75 US GALLONS'. It could be a tick selecting that size or a line cancelling it; the photograph does not settle which, so no single value is picked out of the four.

The brand is handwritten in marker, 'I Heard Cassarole', below the net-contents list. Two letters needed settling, and both were settled against the handwritten 'STYLE: Double India Pale Ale' line, which is the same hand at the same size - x-height 11 rows there, 11 rows in the brand. Coordinates below are front.jpg pixels; ink is grey below 160 against a page white near 225. Final letter is 'e', not 'u'. Every word on the style line that ends in 'e' - Double, Pale, Ale - ends in one downstroke with a hook leaving near the base to the right and no closing curve. The hand's only 'u', in 'Double' at x 178-183, y 508-518, is the other form: 6 columns wide and already at full width at the top of the letter. The brand's final glyph has ink in only 4 columns above its baseline, x 133-136; x 137 to x 145 is blank paper, grey 217 to 246, on every row from y 466 to y 477, and ink reaches x 139 only at the baseline, y 478-480. There is no room there for this hand's 'u'. Measuring spread - the columns between the rightmost ink in a letter's top half and its rightmost ink overall, over the letter's height - the brand glyph gives 0.27, the certain 'e's of Double, Pale and Ale give 0.20, 0.38 and 0.67, and the certain 'u' gives 0.00. Fifth letter is 'a', not 'e', so the brand is 'Cassarole' and not the ordinary spelling 'Casserole': it is a closed bowl, and the word holds exactly three enclosed counters, centred at x 89.5, x 109 and x 123, which are its two a's and its o. This hand's 'e' encloses nothing. The 'e' in 'Heard' could not be used for any of this; at this resolution the letters of that word run together.
The printed brewery logo reads 'Mash Cult' over 'Brewery' in a handwriting-style face, at the top centre. It is the other name on the collar.
The alcohol statement is part printed, part handwritten: printed 'ALC. / VOL.', then '8.0' in marker, then a printed '%'.
Other handwritten fields: 'BATCH # 003', 'BORN ON: 8/26/26', and 'STYLE: Double India Pale Ale'.

The warning body is in capitals and ends 'HEALTH PROBLEMS' followed by a raised mark, transcribed as a closing double quote. No opening quote appears before the heading. Ink is grey below 170 against a paper near 232. The mark is not a full stop: that line's capitals occupy y 360-364, and the mark occupies only y 360-361, with clean paper at y 362-364 (greys 218 to 238), so it is raised to the top of the capital band and never reaches the baseline. It is a doubled mark rather than a single tick, by comparison with this label's own certain comma after 'MACHINERY' three lines above, which is the same type size and the same two-row height: that comma spans two columns, x 122-123 on y 348-349, and carries about 178 grey-levels of ink; the mark spans three columns, x 54-56 on y 360-361 with its peak at x 55, and carries about 406, roughly double. Both totals take ink as paper minus grey summed over the mark's own columns, with the neighbouring letter's column excluded - the S at x 53 for the mark, the Y at x 121 for the comma.
